tip: Press Ctrl+S while a response streams to freeze the TUI — scroll, read, and copy freely; the chat keeps running underneath.
Esc twice starts the exit — Esc once arms it, Esc again opens the confirm box, and Ctrl+D force-quits without asking.
Ctrl+B moves the current task to the background — it keeps working and reports back when it finishes.
Type /stop to cancel a long task outright. Its work entry is closed, so a restart will not resume it — send the request again for a fresh start.
Ctrl+P and Ctrl+X flip Mercury Code between PLAN and EXECUTE — plan first, execute only what you approved.
Press Ctrl+G (or /code diff) to see exactly what changed on disk before you commit.
Ctrl+N inserts a newline in the input box — describe multi-part changes in one go.
The full transcript lives in your terminal's own scrollback — wheel-scroll it and drag to select text like any other output.
Ctrl+D after a task shows its step log — every command that ran and what it returned.
The completion banner recaps the task: what was done, how many files changed, and the next steps it suggests.
Press ↑ in the input box to walk back through your previous prompts.
/whatsnew shows what changed in this Mercury version, with the release-notes link.
/sessions lists your sessions; /session new starts a clean one without losing the old.
/budget shows and manages your daily token budget — override, reset, or set a new cap.
/permissions switches the session permission mode — allow-all for the session, or ask-me for every change.
/models use <provider> switches the default model — saved across restarts.
Ctrl+D (or /log) prints the last task's step log after it finished.
Ctrl+T toggles balanced and detailed views of tool steps.
Type /code in normal chat to jump into Mercury Code — the full-screen coding TUI in the current directory.
Type / to open the command picker with arrow-key navigation — every command is in there.
Long task? /bg current sends it to the background and /bg list shows what's running.
A task you don't want anymore? /stop ends it immediately — no waiting.
After an update, type /whatsnew — one friendly list of what changed.
Mercury also lives in Telegram — /pair links your account and you can chat from your phone.
/skills lists installed skills; /skills search <query> finds more to install.
/status shows your setup at a glance — provider, budget, channels, skills.
